steps.title: The noble four
steps.body: Alsace's four noble grapes are Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat. They're the only ones allowed in most Grand Cru wines. Riesling is the most planted, giving dry, mineral wines. Gewürztraminer gives lychee and rose; Pinot Gris rich, smoky pear; Muscat dry, grapey wines.

steps.title: The others
steps.body: Pinot Blanc and Auxerrois make soft, everyday whites and much of Crémant d'Alsace. Sylvaner gives light, fresh wines. Pinot Noir is the only red, increasingly serious. Edelzwicker and Gentil are blends of several grapes. Most Alsace wines are single-variety, unoaked or aged in old, large foudres.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its character.
steps.explanation: Alsace names each wine by grape.

steps.body: Alsace Muscat is usually dry, a surprise for those who know sweet Muscats. It's a classic with asparagus in spring.

steps.prompt: Which is Alsace's most planted noble grape?
steps.explanation: Riesling covers the most area of the four.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat are noble
Pinot Blanc, Sylvaner and Pinot Noir complete the range
Most wines are single-variety and named by grape
